Consult Summary:
- 35-year-old male lawyer with new-onset, work-associated frontal headaches plus intermittent palpitations, shortness of breath at rest, bilateral hand tingling, reduced appetite, ~5 lb unintentional weight loss, and decreased libido since a recent job change; history of thyroid disease on thyroxine. Plan: in-person exam and thyroid blood tests.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Intermittent severe headaches; episodic palpitations; shortness of breath while at rest (at desk); bilateral hand tingling; reduced appetite; decreased libido; mild unintentional weight loss (~5 lb).
- Symptom timeline/onset: Symptoms began around the time of a recent job change (exact date not provided).
- Pattern/progression: 
  - Headaches occur mostly at work during meetings or while on laptop; not typically during commute; random episodes, symptoms usually occur one at a time rather than all together.
  - Palpitations occur about once daily or more; sometimes noted when entering an elevator in the morning.
  - Shortness of breath occurs at rest at desk; not with exercise.
  - Tingling affects both hands; described as brief “quick pricking”; no leg involvement.
- Location/character (headache): Mostly frontal; does not radiate.
- Associated symptoms: Mild nausea during headaches; reduced appetite; ~5 lb unintentional weight loss; decreased libido since job change.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Not clearly identified; headaches linked to work tasks (meetings, computer use).
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No typical headaches prior to this period.
  - No shortness of breath with exercise.
  - No leg tingling.
  - Weight loss not noticeable in clothing; no external comments about weight change.
- Additional notes:
  - Initial note referenced “feeling hot,” but patient did not endorse this; instead emphasized intermittent shortness of breath (conflict noted).

Past Medical History:
- Thyroid disease:
  - Patient states “hyperthyroidism.”
  - Medication: Thyroxine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Adherence: Reports taking medication as prescribed.
  - Conflict noted: Thyroxine is typically used for hypothyroidism; patient-stated diagnosis is hyperthyroidism.

Medications:
- Thyroxine (dose/route/frequency not documented). Patient reports adherence.

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Social History:
- Occupation: Lawyer; works in London; significant reading, mix of meetings and computer work (~50/50).
- Recent change of job; symptoms began thereafter.
- Stress: Rates current work-related stress ~7–8/10; high-pressure environment typical for role.
- Alcohol: About once weekly; a couple of glasses of wine.
- Tobacco: Denies smoking.
- Recreational drugs: Denies (including cocaine, marijuana).
- Sexual: Reports decreased libido since job change.

Family History:
- Not mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed (telehealth visit).

Investigations:
- None completed during this consult.
- Planned: Blood tests “for your thyroxine” (thyroid function testing planned; specific tests not detailed).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Recurrent frontal headaches, work-associated, with mild nausea
  - Plan: In-person clinic assessment; no medications to be started before examination.
- Issue 2: Intermittent palpitations and shortness of breath at rest (not with exertion)
  - Plan: In-person examination focusing on heart and breathing.
- Issue 3: Bilateral hand tingling
  - Plan: Evaluate in person during clinic visit.
- Issue 4: Reduced appetite and ~5 lb unintentional weight loss
  - Plan: Obtain thyroid-related blood tests as part of evaluation.
- Issue 5: Thyroid disease on thyroxine; diagnosis label conflicting with therapy
  - Plan: Thyroid blood tests to assess control; reconcile diagnosis after results.
- Issue 6: Decreased libido since job change
  - Plan: Address during in-person review; consider relation to stress and thyroid status after evaluation.
- General plan:
  - Patient to book an in-person appointment via the app.
  - Clinician will forward today’s history to the in-person team to avoid repetition.
  - No new medications prescribed pending in-person assessment and labs.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Allergies not documented.
  - Medication dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Vitals and physical examination not performed (telehealth).
  - Red flag screening (fever, focal neuro deficits, chest pain, syncope, visual aura/vision changes) not fully documented.
  - Exact onset date and duration of each symptom not fully specified.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Triage note referenced “feeling hot,” patient did not confirm; instead emphasized intermittent shortness of breath.
  - Patient reports “hyperthyroidism” but is taking thyroxine, typically used for hypothyroidism (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Some audio gaps/inaudible segments and hesitations; DOB not clearly stated; otherwise sufficient to outline key concerns and plan.
